steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).
Pour melted butter into a 9x13-inch dish. Sprinkle graham crumbs evenly over butter; top with chopped nuts, and chocolate chips.
Top with flaked coconut and condensed milk.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden, about 25 minutes. Cool for 15 minutes; cut into finger-length bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Magic Cookie Bars
raw_recipe.description: This magic bars recipe has layers of graham crackers, nuts, chocolate chips, and sweet coconut with results so delicious, you’ll think it’s magic.
raw_recipe.name: Magic Cookie Bars

review.reviewBody:
This has been my absolute favorite treat since I was a small child. This recipe has been passed down from generation to generation and I love it! Although, the recipe my family has is a little bit different than this one...

Tips - Mix the margarine/butter and graham cracker crumbs together to make a firmer "crust". (My family also melts the margarine in the pan in the oven.)

- Pour the condensed milk on the graham cracker crumbs BEFORE adding the other ingredients. It seems to make everything stick together better and it makes it so much more presentable!

- Use more than 1 cup of chocolate chips. Especially if you're a chocolate lover. 1 cup just isn't enough!

Also, I like the recipe better without the nuts. They seem to kind of take away from the other flavors. But I'm not a big fan of nuts in desserts to begin with.

Hope you enjoy these as much as I do! :)

Double the crust, but not the butter. You really only need about 3/4 C. butter/marg if doubling the crust. Thoroughly mix, then press into pan. Pour 1/2 can condensed milk on crust, layer remaining ingredients as directed, and top with remaining 1/2 can of condensed milk. I also doubled the chips and did 1/2 chocolate, 1/2 butterscotch. These disappeared almost immediately at my company's holiday bake sale.

This is so delicious! The only reason I gave this 4 stars is because the recipe calls for sprinkling the crumbs. You have to create a crust on the pan and I poured the condensed milk with each layer so everything was nicely layered together without falling apart.

I used these tips from another reviewer:
Tips - Mix the margarine/butter and graham cracker crumbs together to make a firmer "crust". (My family also melts the margarine in the pan in the oven.)
 
 - Pour the condensed milk on the graham cracker crumbs BEFORE adding the other ingredients. It seems to make everything stick together better and it makes it so much more presentable!
 
 - Use more than 1 cup of chocolate chips.

LOVED IT! I followed one of the reviewers tips which made the recipe better. I doubled the graham cracker crumbs and added 3/4 cup of butter and mixed in a bowl first, then added it to the glass baking pan and pressed it down. I heated up the condensed milk in the microwave to make it more spreadable and poured half onto the graham cracker crust. Then added chocolate chips cookies, walnuts and shredded sweetened coconut (that's what I had on hand) and then poured the remainder of the sweetened condensed milk on top. My friends and coworkers loved it! So easy to make too (:

These were so delicious! We couldn't stop eating them. I mixed the margarine and crumbs before adding it to the pan. I added some more graham cracker crumbs, about 2 1/2 cups total and didn't pour the entire can of milk, just left about a quarter out. it took me some strength to cut these up into bars and take them out of the pan. Will make these again, for sure! thanks!

I made this recipe twice and think potentially with a 3rd try and further modifications, it could be perfect. The first time, I made the recipe as instructed. Sprinkling the graham cracker crumbs over the butter did not form a crust and impossible to use these as "bars". Topping with the condensed milk also made for not the most attractive dish. On round two, I combined the butter and graham cracker crumbs and pressed the crust into the pan, baked it for 10 mins. Based off a couple of reviews, I tried combining the milk, nuts and chocolate chips and layering it all in one swoop. That worked a bit better for appearance but it still didn't "set" quite as nicely and required chilling in the fridge for a bit prior to cutting. I may have needed to increase the baking time a bit. In the future, I'll try one of the recommendations of pouring 1/2 the milk on top of the crust and the remaining on top. I'd give this recipe 3-4 stars based on the instructions/method but 5 for taste.

The only change I made was to increase the crust. I used 2 sticks of butter and about 3/4 of the box of graham crackers. I love the buttery crust and it pairs so nicely with the sweets on top of it. I also layered it the same as another review suggested with half of the condensed milk on top of the crust and the rest right below the coconut. It turned out really well.

I loved these bars! But mix the crumbs and melted butter thoroughly. I've never seen a recipe telling you to sprinkle the crumbs over the melted butter. For the topping, you can add a little more of one and a little less of another. It all depends on what you like. For mine, I added more chocolate and decreased the nuts. I also poured the condensed milk directly on the crumb base. After adding the toppings, I pressed the toppings down gently. After baking, the bars seemed so soft. I thought it maybe didn't turn out. But it firmed up after cooling.
I've been making these since I was a girl [50+ years ago]. The original recipe was on the can of Eagle Brand Sweetened Condensed Milk. The recipe calls for 1 cup chopped nuts - so use your favorite.

I made these as a surprise for coworkers (because I'm cleaning out the cupboards and needed to use that can of sweetened condensed milk!) As others recommended, I mixed the graham crackers and butter together (in a food processor) before pressing into the pan, and I actually used two 9x9" pans instead one of 9x13" without changing the proportions of anything. I used pecans as the nuts, poured the condensed milk over the crust first and pressed everything else into it. It overbaked a little in my oven so the coconut was a little too brown, but it was still pretty good in that salty/sweet/crunchy taste and they disappeared quickly at work.

I loved this recipe, because not only was it so easy to make, but it tasted absolutely delicious. Definitely a must-try. The only difference is that instead of putting walnuts, I put pecans. I really love that touch, because I am not a big fan of walnuts. Overall, love this dessert, and I rate it a 10 out of 10!!
Delicious and simple to make. It’s always a great TREAT!
Love this recipe
My mom made this recipe growing up. She tweaked a bit and added butterscotch chips too. I follow that recipe. Such a great treat! My dad even asked for them today. 😄

These are similar to what are often called Yes-Yes cookie bars (popular in Montreal, among other places). I like to use cookie mix for the base: 1 bag oatmeal or sugar cookie mix, 1 stick of butter cut into the mix, and 1 egg beaten and then added. Press in the bottom of the 9 x 13 pan and bake for 10 -15 minutes before putting on the other ingredients. And I add toffee chips along with mini chocolate chips.
Childhood Christmas cookie
Love this recipe! Made it many times. Easy to follow and definitely delicious. One of my family's favorite!
Easy and delicious!
